example.gloss: The owner said: please come in and sit down.

vocab.gloss: to go out; to come out; to occur

example.hanzi: 我昨天沒出去，在家看電視。
example.pinyin: Wǒ zuótiān méi chūqù, zài jiā kàn diànshì.
example.gloss: I didn't go out yesterday; I watched TV at home.

example.pinyin: Qǐng guān mén, wàimiàn hěn lěng.
example.gloss: Please close the door, it's cold outside.

example.pinyin: Wàimiàn xià yǔ le, jìde dài sǎn.
example.gloss: It's raining outside; remember to take an umbrella.

vocab.gloss: to reach; to arrive; to leave for; to go to; to (a place); until (a time); up to (a point)

example.pinyin: Wǒ qī diǎn bàn dào jiā.
example.gloss: I get home at seven thirty.

example.pinyin: Wǒ cóng jiéyùn zhàn zǒu dào xuéxiào.
example.gloss: I walk from the MRT station to school.

grammar.title: 從 A 到 B — from A to B
grammar.pattern: Subject + 從 + starting point + 到 + destination + (Verb)
grammar.explanation: 從 marks where something starts and 到 marks where it ends. Both phrases come before the verb, or 到 can attach right after a movement verb (走到、搭車到). Use this pattern for places (從台北到台中) and also for times (從早上到晚上).
grammar.contrast: Easily confused with using 到 alone: 我到台北 only names the destination. Add 從 when you also want to say where you set out from; if the starting point is already clear, just drop 從.
grammar.common_error: Learners copy English word order and put the 從-phrase after the verb: ✗我走從家到學校 / ✗我來從台北. In Chinese the 從-phrase goes before the verb: 我從台北來.

examples.hanzi: 我從家裡走到捷運站，要十分鐘。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ cóng jiā lǐ zǒu dào jiéyùn zhàn, yào shí fēnzhōng.
examples.gloss: It takes ten minutes to walk from my place to the MRT station.

examples.hanzi: 他從外面進來，門也沒關。
examples.pinyin: Tā cóng wàimiàn jìnlái, mén yě méi guān.
examples.gloss: He came in from outside and didn't even close the door.

examples.pinyin: Cóng zhèlǐ dào xuéxiào bù yuǎn.
examples.gloss: It's not far from here to school.

dialogue.speaker: 小安
dialogue.pinyin: Wéi, wǒ dào nǐ jiā ménkǒu le.
dialogue.gloss: Hello? I'm at your front door.

dialogue.speaker: 小明

dialogue.gloss: OK, I'll open the door — come in and sit down.

dialogue.speaker: 小安
dialogue.hanzi: 外面雨很大喔！我從捷運站走到這裡，走了十分鐘。
dialogue.pinyin: Wàimiàn yǔ hěn dà o! Wǒ cóng jiéyùn zhàn zǒu dào zhèlǐ, zǒu le shí fēnzhōng.
dialogue.gloss: It's raining hard outside! I walked here from the MRT station — ten minutes.

dialogue.speaker: 小明
dialogue.pinyin: Jìnlái hē yì bēi rè chá ba.
dialogue.gloss: Come in and have a cup of hot tea.

dialogue.speaker: 小安
dialogue.hanzi: 謝謝！晚一點我們出去吃麵，好嗎？
dialogue.pinyin: Xièxie! Wǎn yìdiǎn wǒmen chūqù chī miàn, hǎo ma?
dialogue.gloss: Thanks! Let's go out later for noodles, OK?

dialogue.speaker: 小明
dialogue.hanzi: 好喔，門外那家麵店很近。
dialogue.pinyin: Hǎo o, mén wài nà jiā miàn diàn hěn jìn.
dialogue.gloss: Sure, that noodle shop just outside is very close.

sentences.gloss: I leave the house at seven every day.

sentences.pinyin: Tā cóng Táizhōng dāchē dào Táiběi.
sentences.gloss: He takes a bus from Taichung to Taipei.

sentences.pinyin: Mén wàimiàn yǒu hěn duō rén.
sentences.gloss: There are a lot of people outside the door.
The MRT has arrived at the station.
The owner says please come in and have a seat.

passage.title: 週末的早上
passage.hanzi: 週末早上，我從家裡出門，走到附近的捷運站。外面的天氣很好，不太熱。我先買了一杯珍珠奶茶，再搭捷運到台北。十二點，我進了一家小麵店，老闆笑笑說：請進！外面人很多，裡面很安靜。吃飽以後，我出來走到書店，逛了一個鐘頭。
passage.gloss: On the weekend morning I left home and walked to the nearby MRT station. The weather outside was lovely, not too hot. First I bought a cup of bubble tea, then took the MRT to Taipei. At twelve I went into a small noodle shop; the owner smiled and said, "Come in!" There were lots of people outside, but it was quiet inside. After eating my fill, I came out and walked to a bookshop, where I browsed for an hour.

example.pinyin: Wǒ jiā lí jiéyùn zhàn hěn jìn.
example.gloss: My home is very close to the MRT station.

vocab.gloss: to leave; to part from; to be away from

example.hanzi: 學校離我家不遠,走路就到。
example.pinyin: Xuéxiào lí wǒ jiā bù yuǎn, zǒulù jiù dào.
example.gloss: The school isn't far from my home; you can walk there.

example.hanzi: 我每天走路去學校,路上有一家早餐店。
example.pinyin: Wǒ měi tiān zǒulù qù xuéxiào, lù shàng yǒu yì jiā zǎocān diàn.
example.gloss: I walk to school every day; there's a breakfast shop on the way.

vocab.gloss: towards; to face; to turn towards

example.hanzi: 向前走五分鐘就到郵局了。
example.pinyin: Xiàng qián zǒu wǔ fēnzhōng jiù dào yóujú le.
example.gloss: Walk straight ahead for five minutes and you'll reach the post office.

example.hanzi: 搭捷運很快,十分鐘就到了。
example.pinyin: Dā jiéyùn hěn kuài, shí fēnzhōng jiù dào le.
example.gloss: Taking the MRT is fast — you get there in ten minutes.

vocab.gloss: (after a suppositional clause) in that case; then; (after a clause of action) as soon as; immediately after; (same as 是) merely; nothing else but; simply; just; precisely; exactly

example.pinyin: Tā yí dào jiā jiù shuì le.
example.gloss: He went to sleep as soon as he got home.

grammar.title: Saying how far apart two places are: A 離 B 很近/很遠
grammar.pattern: A + 離 + B + 很近 / 很遠 / 不遠 / 有多遠
grammar.explanation: 離 marks the gap between two points. Put the place you are talking about first (A), then 離, then the reference point (B), and finish with a word describing the distance: 很近, 很遠, 不遠. 離 is not a verb of motion — the sentence describes a static distance, so no 是 is needed before 很近/很遠. You often add a follow-up with 就: 我家離學校很近,走路五分鐘就到了。
grammar.contrast: 從…到… also links two places, but it describes a trip: 從我家到學校要三十分鐘 (how long the journey takes). Use 離 when you are stating the distance between them (我家離學校很近). If the sentence has a verb of going/travelling, use 從…到…; if it ends in 近/遠, use 離.
grammar.common_error: Learners drop 離 and say 我家很近學校, or swap in 從 and say 我家從學校很近. They also insert 是 (我家離學校是很近). Say 我家離學校很近 — 離 + place, then 很近/很遠, with no 是.

examples.hanzi: 我家離捷運站很近,走路五分鐘就到了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiā lí jiéyùn zhàn hěn jìn, zǒulù wǔ fēnzhōng jiù dào le.
examples.gloss: My home is close to the MRT station; it's a five-minute walk.

examples.pinyin: Nà jiā miàn diàn lí zhèlǐ yuǎn ma?
examples.gloss: Is that noodle shop far from here?

examples.hanzi: 郵局離這裡不遠,向前走就看到了。
examples.pinyin: Yóujú lí zhèlǐ bù yuǎn, xiàng qián zǒu jiù kàndào le.
examples.gloss: The post office isn't far from here — walk straight ahead and you'll see it.

dialogue.speaker: 女生
dialogue.pinyin: Qǐngwèn, yóujú lí zhèlǐ yuǎn ma?
dialogue.gloss: Excuse me, is the post office far from here?

dialogue.speaker: 路人
dialogue.hanzi: 不遠喔,向前走就看得到。
dialogue.pinyin: Bù yuǎn ō, xiàng qián zǒu jiù kàn de dào.
dialogue.gloss: Not far at all — just walk straight ahead and you'll see it.

dialogue.speaker: 女生
dialogue.gloss: How many minutes does it take on foot?

dialogue.speaker: 路人
dialogue.pinyin: Wǔ fēnzhōng jiù dào le, hěn jìn.
dialogue.gloss: You'll be there in five minutes — it's very close.

dialogue.speaker: 女生
dialogue.hanzi: 那我騎腳踏車會不會快一點?
dialogue.pinyin: Nà wǒ qí jiǎotàchē huì bú huì kuài yìdiǎn?
dialogue.gloss: Then would it be faster if I rode a bike?

dialogue.speaker: 路人
dialogue.hanzi: 路這麼近,走路就好了啦!
dialogue.pinyin: Lù zhème jìn, zǒulù jiù hǎo le la!
dialogue.gloss: It's such a short way — just walk!

sentences.pinyin: Wǒ jiā lí jiéyùn zhàn hěn jìn.
sentences.gloss: My home is very close to the MRT station.

sentences.pinyin: Xiàng qián zǒu wǔ fēnzhōng jiù dào le.
sentences.gloss: Walk straight ahead for five minutes and you're there.

sentences.pinyin: Wǒ měi tiān zǒulù qù xuéxiào.
sentences.gloss: I walk to school every day.

sentences.pinyin: Dā jiéyùn bǐ qí jiǎotàchē kuài.
sentences.gloss: Taking the MRT is faster than riding a bike.

sentences.pinyin: Tā yí dào jiā jiù shuì le.
sentences.gloss: He went to sleep as soon as he got home.

passage.title: 我的上學路
passage.hanzi: 我家在台北,離捷運站很近,走路五分鐘就到了。每天早上,我先走路到站裡,再搭捷運去學校。捷運很快,七點半出門,八點就到學校了。週末的時候,我喜歡騎腳踏車,從家裡向東騎,一路上有很多小店,還有一家很好吃的麵店。
passage.gloss: My home is in Taipei, very close to the MRT station — a five-minute walk and I'm there. Every morning I walk to the station first, then take the MRT to school. The MRT is fast: I leave at seven thirty and I'm at school by eight. On weekends I like to ride my bike, heading east from home. There are lots of little shops along the way, and a really tasty noodle place too.

example.hanzi: 我在準備明天出門的東西。
example.pinyin: Wǒ zài zhǔnbèi míngtiān chūmén de dōngxi.
example.gloss: I'm getting ready the things for going out tomorrow.

vocab.gloss: to play; to have fun; to trifle with

example.hanzi: 週末我們去台北玩，好不好？
example.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒmen qù Táiběi wán, hǎo bù hǎo?
example.gloss: Let's go to Taipei to have fun this weekend, okay?
Today was really happy — thank you all.

vocab.gloss: to hope; a hope; a wish

example.pinyin: Wǒ xīwàng míngtiān bú huì xià yǔ.
example.gloss: I hope it won't rain tomorrow.

vocab.gloss: bar (loanword) (serving drinks, or providing Internet access etc); to puff (on a pipe etc); (onom.) bang

example.hanzi: 我們一起騎腳踏車去吧！
example.pinyin: Wǒmen yìqǐ qí jiǎotàchē qù ba!

grammar.title: Making a suggestion with 吧
grammar.explanation: Put 吧 at the end of a sentence to turn it into a soft suggestion or a gentle push: 'let's ...' or 'why don't you ...'. It is not a question — you are not really asking, you are proposing. With 我們 it means 'let's', with 你 it means 'go ahead and ...'. In Taiwan 吧 is said lightly and makes the sentence sound friendly instead of bossy.
grammar.contrast: 嗎 vs 吧: 我們去玩嗎？ is a real yes/no question (you have no idea what the other person wants). 我們去玩吧！ is a suggestion (you already want to go and are inviting them). If you expect an answer, use 嗎; if you are proposing, use 吧.
grammar.common_error: Learners often stack the two particles and say 我們去玩嗎吧, or use 嗎 when they mean 'let's'. A sentence can end with only one of them, and an invitation takes 吧, never 嗎.

examples.pinyin: Tài rè le, hē bēi bīng de ba.
examples.gloss: It's too hot — let's have a cold drink.
Why don't you get ready first.

grammar.title: 希望 + clause (hoping something happens)
grammar.explanation: 希望 is followed by a whole sentence, not by a noun. You say 我希望明天是晴天, literally 'I hope tomorrow is a sunny day'. The thing hoped for is usually in the future, so words like 明天、週末 often appear after it.
grammar.contrast: 想 vs 希望: 我想去玩 says what you yourself want to do; 我希望你去玩 says you hope about something you cannot control. Use 想 for your own plan, 希望 for wishes about weather, other people, or results.
grammar.common_error: Saying 我希望好天氣 (hope + noun). 希望 needs a full clause: 我希望天氣很好。

examples.hanzi: 我希望這個週末不會有颱風。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xīwàng zhè ge zhōumò bú huì yǒu táifēng.
examples.gloss: I hope there won't be a typhoon this weekend.

examples.pinyin: Tā xīwàng nǐ jīntiān hěn kuàilè.

examples.hanzi: 我希望我們能一起出門玩。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xīwàng wǒmen néng yìqǐ chūmén wán.
examples.gloss: I hope we can go out and have fun together.

dialogue.speaker: 小文
dialogue.hanzi: 明天是週末，我們出去玩吧！
dialogue.pinyin: Míngtiān shì zhōumò, wǒmen chūqù wán ba!
dialogue.gloss: Tomorrow's the weekend — let's go out and have fun!

dialogue.speaker: 小安
dialogue.hanzi: 好，我想去台北逛逛，還想喝珍珠奶茶。
dialogue.pinyin: Hǎo, wǒ xiǎng qù Táiběi guàng guàng, hái xiǎng hē zhēnzhū nǎichá.
dialogue.gloss: Sure, I'd like to walk around Taipei, and I also want bubble tea.

dialogue.speaker: 小文
dialogue.hanzi: 那我們搭捷運去，早上九點在站前見。
dialogue.pinyin: Nà wǒmen dā jiéyùn qù, zǎoshang jiǔ diǎn zài zhàn qián jiàn.
dialogue.gloss: Then let's take the MRT; see you at nine in front of the station.

dialogue.speaker: 小安
dialogue.gloss: Do I need to prepare anything?

dialogue.speaker: 小文
dialogue.hanzi: 帶悠遊卡就好。希望明天不會下雨。
dialogue.pinyin: Dài yōuyóukǎ jiù hǎo. Xīwàng míngtiān bú huì xià yǔ.
dialogue.gloss: Just bring your EasyCard. I hope it won't rain tomorrow.

dialogue.speaker: 小安
dialogue.hanzi: 我也希望！明天會很好玩。
dialogue.pinyin: Wǒ yě xīwàng! Míngtiān huì hěn hǎowán.
dialogue.gloss: Me too! Tomorrow will be a lot of fun.

sentences.pinyin: Wǒmen zhōumò yìqǐ chūmén wán ba.
sentences.gloss: Let's go out and have fun together this weekend.

sentences.pinyin: Zhè ge zhōumò wǒ zhēn kuàilè.
sentences.gloss: I was really happy this weekend.

sentences.pinyin: Wǒmen dā jiéyùn qù wán ba.
sentences.gloss: Let's take the MRT there to have fun.

passage.title: 週末出門玩
passage.hanzi: 這個週末，我和朋友要一起出門玩。我們早上八點在捷運站見面，先去台北逛逛，中午吃便當，下午喝珍珠奶茶。昨天晚上我就準備好了，帶了悠遊卡、錢和雨傘。希望明天天氣很好，不會下雨，那一天一定會很快樂。
passage.gloss: This weekend I'm going out to have fun with a friend. We'll meet at the MRT station at eight in the morning, first walk around Taipei, eat lunch boxes at noon, and drink bubble tea in the afternoon. I already got ready last night — I packed my EasyCard, money and an umbrella. I hope the weather will be nice tomorrow and it won't rain; that day is sure to be a very happy one.
